L01.note: -9, -36, -144 form a x4 chain; -9 is the generator the other two look derived from.

L02.note: Two reciprocal pairs (11/3 vs 3/11, 11/4 vs 4/11) - perfectly symmetric, no discriminator.

L03.note: 3 generates the set: -3 is its sign twin, 6 = 2x3, 9 = 3x3.

L04.note: 14 is the odd magnitude but nothing selects among 5, -2, -3.

L06.note: 5, 15, 45 are a x3 chain; 53/9 is the only value not reachable from it and the only non-integer.

L07.note: -2, -4, -8, -16 is a closed power-of-two ladder with no odd member.

L08.note: 3 / -3 sign-twin pair usually brackets the key; took the positive.

L09.note: 4, 32, 128 are powers of two and 128 = 4 x 32, so it is built from the others; 36 is the only outsider.

L10.note: 24/5 and 24/7 are a same-numerator denominator pair, the usual key/distractor shape; 36 = 6^2 is a derived trap.

L11.note: 0 and 10 look like boundary traps but -3 vs -2 is undecidable.

L12.note: 3, 4, 5, 6 consecutive integers - no structure to read.

L13.note: all multiples of 3, evenly spread; no signal.

L14.note: -19.5 is the only non-integer and the only value not a multiple of 4; the odd format reads as the computed answer.

L15.note: 27 = 3^3 pairs with 3 but neither is favoured.

L16.note: -9/5 is the only negative and the most 'computed' looking, but 5/6 is an equally plausible fraction key.

L17.note: off-by-one pairs (13,14) and (3,4); the pairs cancel each other out.

L18.note: 8 / -8 sign-twin pair with 16 = 2x8 derived from it; took the positive twin.

L19.note: 400 is the round trap next to 403; 1200 = 3x400 and 120 are scale errors, so the exact-looking 403 is the key.

L20.note: three halves and one integer; the .5 family holds the answer but which one is unreadable.

L21.note: 1,2,3,4 is a how-many-solutions set; 2 is the modal answer for such items.

L22.note: all values are thirds (9 = 27/3); 29/3 is the extreme but that is weak.

L23.note: 26/3 / -26/3 sign-twin pair; -2/3 and 10/3 look like partial-work leftovers.

L24.note: 11 is the odd magnitude; -1 and -2 are adjacent traps, 4 chosen weakly.

L27.note: quarter-denominator values point at a completing-the-square minimum; -209/4 is the messiest, least guessable-by-accident value.

L28.note: 14 and 21 share a factor of 7 but nothing separates them.

L31.note: reciprocal pair 3/2 and 2/3 plus a 5/2, 5/3 pair; symmetric, no read.

L32.note: 1 / -1 sign twin with -16 as an odd magnitude; twin choice is a coin flip.
